paper.title_en: Testing quantum gravity with cold atoms: A quantum-information method
paper.abstract_en: We investigate the interface between quantum mechanics and gravity employing techniques from quantum information theory. The focus is primarily on investigating the gravitationally mediated entanglement (measured here by the concurrence) between two probe qubits created by two-level atoms with a reservoir consisting of thermally equilibrated homogeneous three-dimensional Bose-Einstein condensates. Our results demonstrate that below a certain temperature, the gravitational contribution to the qubit-reservoir interaction may strongly modify their coherence and entanglement dynamics even at large interqubit distance. By analyzing multi-parameter estimation techniques such as the quantum Fisher information, and quantum signal-to-noise ratio as a metric for certifying quantum effects and sensing performance, we show that the spatial separation between qubits and gravitational interaction may enhance estimation efficiency, providing a high-precision quantum gravity sensor.
